Thénardier's Inn, MontfermeilLes MisérablesSteal the bread, keep the silver, and check the innkeeper's bill twice.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersValjean's loaf with salted butter and radishesA crackling, dark-crusted country loaf torn at the table, with salted butter, crisp radishes and salt flakesHow to make it500g bread flour, plus extra for dusting7g dried yeast10g salt400ml warm water125g salted butter, softened1 bunch radishes, trimmed1 tsp salt flakesMix the flour, yeast, salt and warm water to a shaggy, sticky dough. No kneading.Cover and leave to rise until doubled and bubbly.Tip onto a well floured bench, fold the edges in to make a round and set it seam side down on floured baking paper.Heat the oven to 240°C with a lidded cast iron pot inside while the loaf rests.Lift the loaf on its paper into the hot pot, slash the top and bake with the lid on, then lid off until dark and crusty.Cool on a rack, then tear and serve with the butter, radishes and salt flakes.Montfermeil inn pork rillettesPork belly slow-cooked with garlic and thyme until it falls apart, shredded into its own fat, with toasted baguette, cornichons and mustardHow to make it800g pork belly, skin removed, in 3cm cubes2 tsp salt1 tsp black pepper4 garlic cloves, peeled2 bay leaves4 sprigs of thyme200ml water1 baguette, sliced and toasted16 cornichons2 tbsp Dijon mustardHeat the oven to 150°C. Toss the pork with the salt and pepper in a small lidded casserole with the garlic, bay, thyme and water.Cover and cook slowly until the meat falls apart and sits in its own fat.Pick out the herbs, then shred the pork and garlic with two forks, working in enough of the fat to make it soft and spreadable.Pack into jars or a bowl, pour the rest of the fat over the top and chill until set.Serve at room temperature with the toasted baguette, cornichons and mustard.MainsThénardier's inn coq au vinChicken thighs braised in red wine with smoky bacon, eschalots, mushrooms and thyme, with buttery boiled potatoesHow to make it1.5kg bone-in chicken thighs, skin on150g smoked bacon lardons12 eschalots, peeled250g button mushrooms2 garlic cloves, crushed2 tbsp plain flour750ml red wine250ml chicken stock2 bay leaves4 sprigs of thymesalt and pepper, to taste800g small waxy potatoes30g butter2 tbsp parsley, choppedFry the lardons in a large heavy casserole until crisp, then lift out.Season the chicken and brown it well in the bacon fat in batches, skin side first. Lift out.Brown the eschalots and mushrooms in the same pot.Stir in the garlic and flour, then the wine, stock, bay and thyme. Return the chicken and bacon, cover and simmer gently.Meanwhile boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.Take the lid off and simmer until the sauce coats a spoon.Stir in the butter, scatter with parsley and serve with the potatoes.SweetsLittle Cosette's winter pears with chocolate sauceWhole pears poached in vanilla, cinnamon and orange syrup, with a warm dark chocolate sauceHow to make it1 L water200g caster sugar1 tsp vanilla extract1 cinnamon stick3 strips of orange peel4 firm pears, peeled, stalks on100g dark chocolate, chopped125ml thickened creamSimmer the water, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and orange peel in a saucepan that fits the pears snugly until the sugar dissolves.Add the pears, cover with a circle of baking paper and poach gently, turning now and then, until a knife slides in easily.Cool the pears in the syrup.Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the chocolate and stir until smooth.Stand each pear in a shallow bowl with a spoonful of syrup and pour over the warm chocolate sauce.DrinksABC Café hot spiced wineRed wine warmed with honey, orange, cinnamon, clove and star anise, served steaming in glassesHow to make it750ml red wine250ml water80g honey1 orange, sliced2 cinnamon sticks6 cloves2 star anisesPut everything in a saucepan and warm over low heat, stirring until the honey melts. Do not let it boil.Take off the heat and leave to steep.Ladle into 4 heatproof glasses with a slice of orange in each.
